instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: This procedure covers replacing the brake pads on Segway rental bikes, which requires removing the wheel, installing new pads, torquing the caliper to 7.5 Nm, and verifying the installation with a photo. The service is completed by performing twenty bedding-in stops to ensure proper lever feel and bite before a technician signs off on the release.

draft.title: Segway Rental Brake Pad Replacement and Service
disqualifiers: Fork oil or brake fluid on the brake disc
releases: Safe rental operation of the motorcycle

steps.title: Disassembly and Contamination Inspection
steps.explanation: Removing the wheel and caliper allows access to the pads and ensures the brake disc is inspected for oil or fluid, which would cause catastrophic brake failure.

fields.prompt: Inspect the brake disc for any fork oil or brake fluid contamination.
fields.guidance: The disc must be completely clean. Any presence of fork oil or brake fluid is a disqualifier.

steps.title: Pad Installation and Photo Verification
steps.explanation: Fitting the new pads and taking a photo before the wheel goes back on provides visual proof that the pads are correctly seated in the caliper.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the new pads sitting in the caliper before reinstalling the wheel.
fields.acceptance_description: New brake pads correctly seated inside the caliper.
fields.guidance: Ensure the photo clearly shows the new pads installed in the caliper before the wheel goes back on.

steps.title: Caliper Torque
steps.explanation: Torquing the caliper bolts to exactly 7.5 Nm ensures they are secure and will not back out during operation.

fields.prompt: Torque the caliper bolts to 7.5 Nm and record the value.
fields.guidance: Use a calibrated torque wrench to tighten the caliper bolts to exactly 7.5 Nm.

steps.title: Bedding-In Road Test
steps.explanation: Performing twenty gentle stops beds the pads to the disc, ensuring the lever is firm and the brakes bite correctly before a tourist rides the bike.

fields.prompt: Perform 20 gentle stops down the lane. How does the brake lever feel?
fields.guidance: The lever must feel firm and the brakes must bite properly after the 20 bedding-in stops.

steps.title: Technician Sign-Off
steps.explanation: An authorized technician must sign off to release the bike, taking responsibility for the safety of the rental.

fields.prompt: Sign to certify that the brake service is complete and the bike is safe to release.
fields.guidance: Only authorized technicians may sign off on this brake service.
